sentences.text: The prosecution case is that the informant, who is 18 years old young girl, is daughter of the petitioners co-accused Subhash Rathod.
She has a step-mother.
While the informant wanted to pursue her studies, her uncle and father allegedly sold her for Rs.2,00,000/-.
The informant lived with the petitioner for a period of one month.
She alleged that during that period she was sexually assaulted repeatedly by unknown persons.
Thereafter, she came back to her fathers residence when she was unfortunately again sold firstly to one Sandip Mali and then one Vitthal Gaikwad.
Eventually, she was able to make a complaint on the basis of which the subject FIR was registered.
The petitioner was arrested on 25.09.2021.
She is stated to be an advocate, practicing in the Sessions Court since 2012 and also runs NGO.
3. The investigation is complete; chargesheet has been filed.
Thereafter, charges have also been framed, though the trial is yet to commence.
4. It appears from the counter affidavit, filed by respondents, that two accused persons are absconding due to which the trial is likely to be delayed.

5. Taking into consideration the period already spent by the petitioner in custody, however, without expressing any opinion on the merits of the case, the petitioner is directed to be released on bail subject to her furnishing bail bonds to the satisfaction of the Trial Court.
6. The special leave petition is, accordingly, disposed of.
7. Pending application(s), if any, stands disposed of.

(ARJUN BISHT) (PREETHI T.C.)
COURT MASTER (SH) COURT MASTER (NSH)
